what_its_for: Ramipril is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension) and heart failure. It is also used to lower the risk of heart attack, stroke, and kidney problems, especially in people with diabetes or heart disease. It belongs to a group of medicines called ACE inhibitors, which help relax and widen your blood vessels so your heart does not have to work as hard.
how_to_take: Take ramipril by mouth, with or without food. Swallow the capsule whole with a full glass of water. If you have trouble swallowing it, you may open the capsule and sprinkle the contents into a small amount of applesauce or mix it in water or apple juice — take it right away and do not save it for later. Take your dose at the same time each day to help you remember. Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor first, even if you feel well.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your condition, kidney function, and other medicines you take. For high blood pressure, the usual starting dose is 2.5 mg once a day. For heart failure or heart attack recovery, starting doses may differ. Your doctor may slowly increase your dose over several weeks. Always follow the dose your doctor prescribes — do not take more or less than directed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — unless it is almost time for your next dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store ramipril at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C and 25°C). Keep it away from moisture, heat, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date printed on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid salt substitutes or potassium supplements unless your doctor tells you it is okay — ramipril can raise potassium levels in your blood, which can be dangerous. Avoid alcohol, as it can increase dizziness or lower your blood pressure too much. Be careful when standing up quickly from a sitting or lying position, as ramipril may cause dizziness, especially when you first start taking it. Avoid taking anti-inflammatory pain relievers like ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin) or naproxen (Aleve) without asking your doctor, as they can reduce how well ramipril works and may harm your kidneys. Do NOT take ramipril if you are pregnant — it can cause serious harm or death to an unborn baby.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat (this is called angioedema and can make it hard to breathe — call 911 immediately); signs of high potassium such as muscle weakness, irregular heartbeat, or numbness; signs of kidney problems such as little or no urination, swelling in your legs or feet; dizziness or fainting; a persistent dry cough that bothers you; unusual tiredness or yellowing of the skin or eyes (signs of liver problems); or if you become pregnant while taking this medicine.
when_it_works: Ramipril starts working to lower your blood pressure within a few hours of taking the first dose. However, it may take 2 to 4 weeks of regular use to see the full benefit. Even if you feel fine, keep taking it every day — high blood pressure often has no symptoms, but if left untreated it can cause serious health problems. Do not stop taking it just because you feel better.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Do NOT take ramipril during pregnancy. It can cause serious injury or death to your unborn baby. If you become pregnant, tell your doctor immediately. Breastfeeding: Ramipril may pass into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Children: Ramipril is not commonly used in children; talk to your doctor. Older adults: Older adults may be more sensitive to the blood pressure-lowering effects and may experience more dizziness. Use caution when standing up. Kidney or liver disease: Your doctor may need to adjust your dose if you have kidney or liver problems. Diabetes: If you have diabetes and are also taking aliskiren (Tekturna), do not combine it with ramipril — this combination increases the risk of serious side effects.
